summary: D02 keeps 47 of its 57 nodes, re-scopes the prerequisites of 10 on causal grounds (one at D04's request) and adds 3 nodes (cupellation, percussion_drilling, metallography). Iron-vs-bronze verdict: iron_bloomery's factors match its peers; its closure (10 nodes / 14,320 RP) was cheaper than the A3 CORE fact (9 / 15,250) because its only prerequisite was charcoal, so bloomery smelting needed no furnace knowledge. Proposed iron_bloomery <- charcoal AND kiln_updraft (prereq_complexity 0 -> 0.5 by convention: 8,360 -> 11,830 RP; closure 14 / 26,130). Copper smelting stays an accelerator (the node's own Eureka): requiring it would make that Eureka implied, which the loader refuses, and would deny the debated sub-Saharan route; bellows would fail the chronology test. Other causal fixes: microliths need blade production; lost-wax predates closed moulds and tin bronze, so it rests on open casting; pattern welding needs steel, not tempering; lacquer owes nothing to fermentation; hydraulic concrete needs lime, not the arch; cast iron needs casting and the water-powered blast furnace needs bellows (each replacing a redundant atom, cost unchanged); superalloys rest on scientific metallurgy; aluminium needs industrial alkali for its alumina (D04's request, cost unchanged). New nodes: metallography separates the science of metals from steelmaking; cupellation supplies the silver weighed-silver exchange and fire assay need; percussion drilling is the extraction step of the brine, gas and oil chains (D04 made petroleum_refining processing-only). The bronze chain is documented exactly (MEASURED): ungated copper-ore and tin-ore -> bronze casting gated by tin_bronze -> bronze as the only metal for tools; arsenical bronze opens A3 without any recipe. Identification (cassiterite and others) is requested from D11; extraction-depth gating is an open decision. Net workload +21,230 RP (0.19 % of 11.21M).

MEASURED anomaly resolved on causal grounds. The node's factors match its peers, but its only prerequisite was charcoal, so bloomery smelting - reducing ore with charcoal in a furnace at roughly 1,100-1,300 C - was reachable with no furnace knowledge at all; that missing edge, not the scoring, made its closure (10 nodes / 14,320 RP) cheaper than the A3 CORE fact (9 / 15,250). kiln_updraft (an enclosed firing chamber, controlled atmosphere, 'the thermal precondition for smelting') is the knowledge every centre needed, including the sub-Saharan clay shaft furnaces (INFERENCE: the tree's kiln node stands for building an enclosed high-temperature chamber, which a smelting furnace is). Copper smelting stays an accelerator, not a requirement: the node's own Eureka (when: copper_smelting) says so ('Not a prerequisite: African iron may be independent'); making it a prerequisite would make that Eureka implied, which the loader refuses (Eurekas are append-only), and would deny the debated independent-invention route. Bellows were not used: their emerged (~1,500 BCE) post-dates iron (~1,800 BCE) and the chronology test would fail (D06 request).

existing.prereqRationale: charcoal: the fuel and reductant of every bloomery (existing edge). kiln_updraft: a closed high-temperature chamber holding a reducing atmosphere - without it ore cannot be reduced to a bloom; it is the furnace knowledge shared by the copper-smelting centres (Anatolia, Iran, the Levant, South Asia, China) and by sub-Saharan clay-furnace smelting, whose independence from a copper tradition is debated (reviewed by S. B. Alpern, History in Africa 32, 2005; the early Termit and Nok dates are contested). Not added: copper_smelting (makes the existing Eureka implied; denies the African route), bellows (chronology), an OR of the two (encodes forced draught on one route only and makes the copper route's Eureka automatic).

It is historically right, but MEASURED, only tin_bronze realizes the bronze good - and bronze is the only input of tools - so an arsenical-route polity enters A3 unable to cast bronze or make tools, and cannot meet a3_bronze_stock without tin_bronze or trade. D02 recommends keeping the OR and saying so in the Age panel.

OPEN DECISION (M10+ resources): realize iron_bloomery with an iron-ore deposit good (surface, ungated) and bloomery-smelting and iron-toolmaking recipes, so iron becomes the tin-free route to tools it historically was. Today iron has no production consequence at all.

OPEN DECISION (with the fog lane and D11): if surface ores stay ungated and new deep resources are identification-gated, D02 proposes the extraction ladder mining_shaft (underground lodes above the water table) -> steam_atmospheric (below it) -> dynamite (hard rock at scale), with percussion_drilling for fluids; a pre-steam drainage node (Roman drainage wheels, Agricola 1556) would be added only when deep deposits exist. Who owns the gate - ProductionSystem extraction or the proposed DiscoverySystem?

Package rule: redundant conjuncts (a prerequisite already implied by another, e.g. fired_brick's mudbrick, formerly cast_iron's kiln_updraft and blast_furnace_water's charcoal) inflate prereq_complexity. Should the validator flag them and the convention count only independent requirements?

Historical check requested: (a) casting_closed could take an OR (arsenical_bronze OR tin_bronze) if closed-mould casting of arsenical copper before tin bronze is confirmed; (b) Wagner's view that Chinese casting arose separately in the south could justify a no-bloomery route to cast_iron; neither adopted on the evidence found.

Implied-Eureka trap (MEASURED loader rule 24 + append-only Eurekas): a node whose Eureka condition is a knowledge atom can never take that atom as a prerequisite; three Eurekas read mining_shaft, which blocks mining-depth nodes upstream of steam_atmospheric, railway and dynamite. Should the package let a lane retire a Eureka when it promotes its condition to a prerequisite (needs a save-index rule)?
